column1: # d197_rule.tsv — D197's DECISION RULE for the mfcard window, DECLARED BEFORE ANY NUMBER EXISTS (review 2026-11-15 r5
# memfn-mfindcomb FIDELITY-4, as ruled, with the kit manager's R1 of 2026-11-15 (main's conditions); lane mcfixa).
# D197: the fused inline one-member finder is an unpicked measuring instrument; the timing is ONE-SIDED: a fused
# LOSS to libc memchr settles span_pick row 1 against the finder, a fused WIN triggers building the ruled split
# shape under its own owner go (then a re-measure).
# THE TIMED SHAPE IS INLINE, AS PCREC EMITS IT: each cell's timed function `_time` holds the finder's ONE call site
# with the site inlined (the gate is a separate object; link.py's TIMED-SHAPE check refuses a `_time` calling a
# function its own object defines), as in pcrec's rx_search under `--harness=mfind` (review r5 FIDELITY-1).
# ONE VERDICT PER ISA LEVEL, never one global verdict (R1 (1)). Each `levels` row names the form a pcrec build AT
# THAT LEVEL emits under the lever, CONFIRMED from the kit's selection (lane mcfixa, 2026-11-15, build/pcrec-harness
# --harness=mfind -p rx --pattern 'xy[0-9]+z' and 'foo.*bar': no -fmemfn-simd -> the SWAR body `fn-mfind` = cell
# form mfind-swar (4 `memcpy(&w` loads with the lever, 0 without; stamp `none`, the stamp names SIMD forms only);
# -fmemfn-simd=x86-64 -> `mfind@w16`; -fmemfn-simd=x86-64-v3 -> `mfind@w32+w16` (w32 the timed loop, w16 its
# tail)), compared with libc memchr AS IT RUNS ON THIS BOX: the shipped arm (RUNDIR; the record names the ifunc
# variant bound, `memchr=`; it carries no GLIBC_TUNABLES and names no `avx2`: review r6 FIDELITY-2) and the
# AVX2-tunable arm (RUNDIR.avx2libc; its record must name memchr=avx2) as the second libc row. Each row's `axes`
# names EVERY axis on which its two forms differ (the standing one-variable rule); the libc side's vector is the one
# the arm's RECORD names, printed per arm from `libc_variant` below (never asserted here: r6 RULE-8(b)).
# AXES THE TIMED SHAPE DOES NOT SHARE WITH PRODUCTION (review r6, NOTED; beside D197's one-sidedness above, each a
# named differing axis the verdict carries, none measured): the CALLER LOOP (the cell restarts its tight loop at
# hit+1; pcrec's DFA re-enters at state 0); the HOST FUNCTION's other inlined sites (register pressure: the cell's
# `_time` holds one site, rx_search more; `text_bytes` sizes the timed function only); PLACEMENT (the cell's seeded
# pads vs the artifact's layout); the FIXED compile flags (the slot's, not the user's build); the EVEX libc variant's
# width (the probe names the encoding, not 256 vs 512 bits).
# THE WINDOW RUNS ON THE 7700X (ZEN 4) ONLY (review r7 RULE-3, DOC): the shipped-arm guard below (no-verdict whenever the
# shipped memchr bound `avx2`) encodes that box's ifunc landscape (shipped = EVEX); on an AVX2-only box (the Zen 1)
# the shipped memchr IS avx2, so every level reads INCONCLUSIVE, then NOT-WIN: the guard refuses such a box BY DESIGN.
# The general fix (refuse on tunables alone) is a PLAN item, triggered by the first mfcard window planned off the 7700X.
# THE LIBC ROWS' PROVENANCE ([r5 R3]): the AVX2 row is the process under GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.cpu.hwcaps=-AVX512VL;
# on this box's glibc 2.43 -AVX512F alone STILL binds the EVEX memchr (ymm16; measured by lane mcfixa with
# record.py's probe), so each record names the variant its process bound (`libc ... memchr=`) and the arm table
# refuses an AVX2 record that bound anything else (no-verdict).
# Read by d197_rule.py (`rule RUNDIR AVX2RUNDIR [--second FIRST FIRSTAVX2] [--confirm CRUNDIR CAVX2RUNDIR]`, `drill`). Tables are
# FIRST MATCH, top to bottom; the `when` words are the named predicates d197_rule.py defines (WHEN, one line each).
# STATISTIC (R1 (2)), est.py's units: a find_hit@6 row's x_l = its PER-HIT cost (the cell minus its own miss-only
# base, over the planted hits E: the per-hit slope of cost over hits at fixed length) in ppm of the window's unit W,
# per launch l (7 launches). Per deciding cell, the level's form F against libc L in the SAME record:
#   gain_l  = x_l(L) - x_l(F), the same job, launch and cell (positive: F is cheaper per hit)
#   gain    = med over the 7 launches of gain_l
#   floor   = aa(L) + aa(F), each row's paired A/A (est.py's `aa`: med_l |x_l(twin) - x_l(arm)|): THE A/A FLOOR
#   trimmed = the 7 gain_l less the one farthest from their median (est.py's trim)
# WHY THE SCAN COST NEVER DECIDES ([r5 R3 (3)]): span_pick row 1 picks what a find-then-verify site does AT EACH
# CANDIDATE (the finder continues its mask past a rejected hit, libc restarts a call at hit+1 and checks after it),
# and only the per-hit slope prices that; the miss-only per-byte rate is the search WIDTH, which the level (w16,
# w32, later w64) fixes, not row 1. It is still PRINTED per level beside the verdict (find_byte@6, form and libc,
# their ratio form/libc, both libc rows) so a large scan deficit is visible to whoever reads the verdict.
# The emitted size (EMITTED-1: the lever text 2.9x-6x fn-memchr's body) is reported by est.py rows, never decides.
# LOSSES COUNT OVER THE LEVEL'S 36 COMPARISONS (18 cells x 2 libc rows, a (cell, libc row) pair each; [r5 R3 (1)],
# r6 RULE-8(a)): three or more loss COMPARISONS count at once; a loss resting on one or two comparisons must
# REPRODUCE: their cells get ONE confirming re-run (job 610-kit-mfcard-confirm: a new run id, only those cells, both
# libc arms; plan.py CONFIRM_CELLS, window `mfconfirm`) and count only if they lose again beyond the floor (scored
# with --confirm); one that does not reproduce scores tie. A confirmation is never re-issued: a confirming record
# est REFUSED, mis-bound, or missing a loss cell's rows leaves the level INCONCLUSIVE (r6 RULE-5).
# --confirm re-scores ONLY the levels whose first-pass verdict is CONFIRM; every other level keeps its first-pass
# verdict, so a 3+ LOSS stands at once even when a confirmed cell is shared with another level (r6 R1).
# UNPRICED (the cell table's `either-row-unpriced`; r6 RULE-4): a deciding row is unpriced when est's row is ABSENT,
# its job DRIFTED, or it has no per-launch x (no W). A row est prices NULL or TEXT (est.py's own `unpriced` words)
# still has its per-launch x and is read here: the rule's statistic is its own x and A/A floor, not est's value.
# THE RECORDS (review r6 RULE-2, RULE-3, RULE-6): every record the rule reads PINS this table and d197_rule.py
# (record.py `window`: d197_rule_tsv_sha256, d197_rule_py_sha256) and the rule REFUSES a record whose pin differs
# from the files it runs with; the two arms (and a confirming or first run's two) share code_commit, plan and the
# deciding forms' kit fold hashes; a confirming record is window `mfconfirm`, another run id, and re-ran exactly the
# CONFIRM's cells; `--second FIRST FIRSTAVX2` names the first run's records (window `mfcard`, another run id): a
# second run is derived from those records, never asserted by a bare flag. A refused provenance is no verdict
# (exit 2), never a row.
